key_insight: Automatically generate personalized worked examples by extracting pattern-based Knowledge Components (KCs) from students' code submissions, so examples directly target the specific partial solutions and errors students produce.
problem_solved: Fixed libraries of worked examples often fail to match students' partial solutions and logical errors, forcing heavy authoring effort or coarse, ineffective personalization; this paper solves scalable, fine-grained alignment between student code and instructional examples.
method: Mine large sets of student code submissions to identify recurring solution/error patterns and represent them as pattern-based Knowledge Components (KCs).
Map KCs to parameterized worked-example templates (or generate tailored stepwise explanations) that incorporate the student's own code context.
Evaluate the generated examples against baseline fixed libraries to measure improved relevance and coverage of student misconceptions.
impact: Enables scalable, fine-grained personalization for intelligent tutoring and practice systems, reducing manual authoring and improving the instructional relevance of examples—useful for AI/ML teams building adaptive learning products.
visual_elements: Flow diagram: Student code submission → KC extraction → Template mapping → Personalized worked example
Before/After pair: generic worked example vs. personalized example applied to a student’s partial code
Bar chart or heatmap: improved alignment/coverage of student errors by generated examples vs. fixed library
Icons: code snippet, magnifying glass (pattern mining), puzzle piece (KC), lightbulb (learning gain)
paper_title: Personalized Worked Example Generation from Student Code Submissions using Pattern-based Knowledge Components
paper_authors: Griffin Pitts, Muntasir Hoq, Peter Brusilovsky, Narges Norouzi, Arto Hellas
